patterns.usage_note: Resolving or straining not to do something, most often an involuntary reaction the subject is suppressing (泣くまいとして天井を見ていた); まい is the negative volitional and する supplies the effort. The は of 〜まいとはした marks contrast, conceding the attempt just before reporting that it failed. Godan verbs take the dictionary form (泣くまい), while ichidan and する verbs appear both in full (見るまい) and, in more literary usage, shortened (見まい, すまい). It belongs to narrative and written prose.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]は泣[な]くまいとして天井[てんじょう]をじっと見[み]ていた。
examples.english: Determined not to cry, my little brother kept his eyes fixed on the ceiling.

examples.ruby: 父[ちち]は杖[つえ]に頼[たよ]るまいとして、背筋[せすじ]を伸[の]ばして歩[ある]いた。
examples.english: Set on not leaning on his cane, my father walked with his back straight.

examples.ruby: 余計[よけい]なことは書[か]くまいとはしたが、つい長文[ちょうぶん]になった。
examples.english: I did try to keep the extra remarks out of it, but it still turned into a wall of text.
